holidays.name: National Spinach Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the leafy green that made Popeye's biceps bulge. Sauté it, blend it into a smoothie, or toss it in a salad, and maybe flex in the mirror afterward.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday, popularly tied to the Popeye cartoon legacy. The character first appeared in a comic strip in 1929 and later helped boost spinach sales in the United States.
holidays.funFact: Spinach's reputation for iron is often blamed on a misplaced decimal point in an old nutrition measurement. The story is popular, though historians say it may be partly myth. Spinach does contain iron, just not nearly as much as the legend suggests.

holidays.name: Make Up Your Own Holiday Day
holidays.description: A day when you are encouraged to invent your own holiday and celebrate it however you wish. Rules are optional, and the more ridiculous the holiday, the better.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, modern observance that circulates in lists of quirky holidays. It gives people permission to create their own traditions, such as National Wear Socks on Your Hands Day.
holidays.funFact: Because the holiday is self-referential, anyone who celebrates it automatically celebrates it correctly. It is basically impossible to get wrong.

holidays.name: Purple Day for Epilepsy
holidays.description: People around the world wear purple to raise awareness about epilepsy and to show support for those living with it. Schools, workplaces, and landmarks join in with purple outfits, events, and lighting.
holidays.origin: Founded in 2008 by Cassidy Megan, a young girl from Nova Scotia, Canada, who wanted to start a conversation about epilepsy and reduce the stigma around seizures. The day has since grown into a global movement.
holidays.funFact: Cassidy chose lavender, a flower often linked with isolation and loneliness, to symbolize how people with epilepsy can sometimes feel.

holidays.name: National Nougat Day
holidays.description: A sweet salute to the chewy, nutty confection found in candy bars and festive treats. It is a day to enjoy nougat in all its forms, from soft and fluffy to firm and crunchy.
holidays.origin: An unofficial candy holiday celebrated by confectionery fans. Nougat has a long history in Mediterranean and Middle Eastern sweets, with variations such as Italian torrone and Spanish turrón.
holidays.funFact: Nougat is traditionally made from whipped egg whites, honey or sugar syrup, and nuts. Its texture can range from soft to hard, depending on how long the sugar is cooked.

holidays.name: Prince Kuhio Day
holidays.description: A Hawaii state holiday honoring Prince Jonah Kuhio Kalanianaole, remembered for his service to the Hawaiian people. Celebrations include parades, cultural events, and community festivities.
holidays.origin: Prince Kuhio was born in 1871 and later served as Hawaii's delegate to the U.S. Congress. He is remembered for his work to preserve Hawaiian culture and for supporting the Hawaiian Homes Commission Act.
holidays.funFact: Prince Kuhio is often called the Prince of the People, and he is one of the few royals to have a state holiday named in his honor in the United States.
